$comment: The roles of design §4.1 to §4.6 and the cross-role scenarios of §4.7, one row per heading; check-data.mjs fails when the counts differ. does and risks are the site's short reading of each section; scenario steps follow the document's numbered lists.

roles.name: End user
roles.does: Uses applications. Evaluates an application before using it and watches for degraded service; never touches the protocol directly.
roles.risks: Application bugs, poor channel or connector choices, a channel closed while messages are in flight, and finality risk if a verifier accepts proofs below finality. Escrowed assets should be settled before stopping.

roles.name: Application developer
roles.does: Sends messages and handles the responses in callbacks, naming a channel and a connector on every send. Keeps both configurable, watches connector health and channel status, and migrates when a proof format changes.
roles.risks: Every cross-ledger payload is untrusted input; payloads sit on chain in plaintext unless the application encrypts them; a compromised verifier can mean direct loss of assets.

roles.name: Connector operator
roles.does: Often also creates the channel: deploys a verifier, registers the channel, then registers as a connector on both ledgers. Keeps a balance to pay for execution and a locked stake that covers fines; may run allow-lists and rate limits.
roles.risks: An empty balance fails messages and slashes the stake with escalating penalties; a lapsed registration fails them too; removal is blocked while messages are in flight.

roles.name: Verifier developer
roles.does: An off-chain role with no protocol identity: writes the contract that checks one ledger's proofs. Ledger implementers, connector operators, application developers with high-value flows and auditors all have reasons to.
roles.risks: Proof format changes need new implementations; an upgrade key on a verifier is a single point of compromise; the protocol pays nothing for maintenance.

roles.name: Endpoint operator
roles.does: On Hiero, nothing: every consensus node is an endpoint automatically. Elsewhere, registers with a bond, is admitted by the service admin, serves every channel on the service, and pre-funds the account that submits bundles.
roles.risks: Invalid, failed or duplicate submissions cost unreimbursed fees; misbehaviour means eviction, with the bond returned in full.

roles.name: CLPR Service admin
roles.does: Broad but only protective powers: adjusts the ledger's published limits, admits or evicts endpoints, closes channels and, where the service has a kill switch (the EVM contracts do), turns it on or off. Cannot create channels, register connectors or take part in the economics.
roles.risks: Abuse of power, mitigated by governance; inaction, since a compromised channel left open keeps being exploited; and no in-protocol incentive, a known gap between responsibility and motivation.

scenarios.name: Setting up a new cross-ledger route
steps: A verifier developer publishes and audits a verifier for the target proof system.
A connector operator evaluates it, deploys it, registers the channel on both ledgers, and registers as a connector on both sides.
An application developer evaluates the channel and the connector and integrates them.
End users use the application; the trust chain is active from top to bottom.

scenarios.name: Proof format upgrade
steps: The source ledger announces a proof format upgrade.
A verifier developer publishes a verifier for the new format.
A connector operator creates a new channel with it and registers as a connector.
Application developers migrate to the new channel.
The source ledger switches formats; the old channel's verifier stops working.
The service admin closes the old channel. The source ledger keeps the old format alive long enough for the migration.

scenarios.name: Responding to a compromised verifier
steps: A vulnerability is discovered and a security advisory issued.
The service admin closes the affected channels; their queues drain.
The verifier developer publishes a patched implementation.
Connector operators create new channels with the patched verifier.
Application developers migrate. The window of exposure is between discovery and close.

scenarios.name: Connector withdrawal under load
steps: The connector operator updates its authorization contract to reject all new messages.
Application developers switch to another connector or notify their users.
Once every in-flight message has settled, the operator removes the connector and recovers its funds.
